title: Marcellus (Empiricus), De medicamentis liber (On Remedies) / RU: Марцелл Эмпирик, «О лекарствах»
author: Marcellus of Bordeaux, magister officiorum 394–395
size: Preface, prefatory epistles and 36 chapters arranged head to foot; 255 pp. in Niedermann; est. 90–100k words
edition: Niedermann, CML V (1916; 2nd ed. 1968). Helmreich, Teubner 1889, public domain: https://archive.org/details/marcellidemedic00unkngoog
ru_evidence: ru.wikipedia lists only the German translation. Not in ancientrome, vostlit or simposium. The 1980 anthology 'Медицина в памятниках латинской литературы' may contain excerpts (unverified).
en_evidence: en.wikipedia mentions no translation. Open Library shows only the German translation (1968) and German studies.
other_translations: German complete: Kollesch & Nickel, CML V (Akademie-Verlag 1968). No complete French or Italian found.
value: A unique view of Gallo-Roman everyday medicine, magic and Christianization. Contains Gaulish plant names and charms (important for Celtic studies), links to Ausonius' circle, and preserves earlier Latin pharmacology. Used by historians of medicine, Celticists and Latinists.
ai_feasibility: medium: recipes are formulaic. Plant and drug identification, measures, vulgarisms and charms need an expert lexicographic check.
pilot_unit: Preface, prefatory epistles and Chapter 8 (eye diseases, with charms); est. 12–15k words
